components.note: 木 (wood) — 校 originally related to a wooden framework, later coming to mean 'school,' a place of structured learning
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 校's reading xiào
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.

example.hanzi: 校长在开学典礼上讲话。
example.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng zài kāixué diǎnlǐ shàng jiǎnghuà.
example.english: The principal spoke at the opening ceremony.
example.fact: 校 has two readings — xiào ("school") in 校长 and 学校, and jiào ("to proofread, to compare") in 校对 ("to proofread") — a common trap for learners since the character looks identical in both words.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'
手 (hand) — 拿 means to take or hold something in the hand
合 (hé) gives a sound related to 拿's reading ná, from an older, closer pronunciation link
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'

example.hanzi: 我朋友明年要去加拿大留学。
example.pinyin: Wǒ péngyou míngnián yào qù Jiānádà liúxué.
example.english: My friend is going to study abroad in Canada next year.
example.fact: 加拿大 is a phonetic transliteration of "Canada" with no meaning behind the characters themselves — 加 ("add"), 拿 ("take"), and 大 ("big") were chosen purely for their sounds jiā-ná-dà, a common strategy for rendering foreign place names into Chinese.

components.note: 马 (horse) shows 驾 relates to driving or controlling an animal or vehicle.
加 (jiā) gives a sound close to jià, differing mainly in tone.
马 (horse) — 驶 originally described a horse running swiftly, extending to 'to drive, to sail.'
史 (shǐ) gives the sound — an exact match with 驶.

example.hanzi: 他正在学习驾驶飞机。
example.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài xuéxí jiàshǐ fēijī.
example.english: He is learning to fly (pilot) an airplane.
example.fact: Both characters in 驾驶 carry the horse radical 马 — a reminder that the word predates automobiles and airplanes, having first described controlling a horse-drawn carriage before broadening to any vehicle.

components.note: 入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 医生全力抢救伤者。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng quánlì qiǎngjiù shāngzhě.
example.english: The doctors worked with all their strength to save the injured.
example.fact: 全力 almost always appears as an adverb right before a verb (全力支持 "fully support") rather than standing alone as a noun — the set four-character idiom 全力以赴 ("to go all out") is one of the most common ways to build on it.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
才 (talent) — many talented people.
囗 (an enclosure) — gathered together in one place, giving 团 its meaning 'group, team; round, ball-shaped.'
米 (grain, rice) — 糟 originally named the dregs left over from making rice wine.
曹 (cáo) gives a sound close to zāo, sharing the same rhyme and tone.

example.hanzi: 房间里被弄得一团糟。
example.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ bèi nòng de yìtuánzāo.
example.english: The room was made into a complete mess.
example.fact: 团 contributes its sense of a rounded, clumped mass (also seen in 面团 "dough" and 主席团 "presidium") to 一团糟 — literally "one clump of dregs," picturing disorder as something balled up together rather than merely scattered about.

components.note: 太 adds a small dot below 大 (big) — the extra mark emphasizes something even bigger or more extreme, giving 太 its meaning 'too' or 'extremely.'
穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 中国的太空计划发展很快。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó de tàikōng jìhuà fāzhǎn hěn kuài.
example.english: China's space program is developing quickly.
example.fact: 太空 literally means "extremely empty" (太 "extremely" + 空 "empty, sky") — the same 空 that means "empty" in 空房间 ("empty room") extends naturally to the vast emptiness beyond the atmosphere.

components.note: 屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
疒 (sickness) — relates directly to 病's meaning 'illness, disease, to be sick.'
丙 (bǐng) gives a sound hint — 病 is pronounced bìng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他昨天生病了,没来上班。
example.pinyin: Tā zuótiān shēngbìng le, méi lái shàngbān.
example.english: He got sick yesterday and didn't come to work.
example.fact: 生病 is a verb-object compound built from 生 ("to give rise to, to produce") + 病 ("illness") — literally "to produce sickness" — which is why 病 can still be pulled out and used on its own as a noun (他的病 "his illness") even though 生病 has become the fixed verb for "to fall ill."

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — 适 relates to fitting well as one moves along, i.e. being suitable
舌 (shé) gives a sound distantly related to 适's reading shì, having drifted apart over a long time

example.hanzi: 新学生需要时间适应新环境。
example.pinyin: Xīn xuésheng xūyào shíjiān shìyìng xīn huánjìng.
example.english: New students need time to adapt to a new environment.
example.fact: 应 here is read yìng ("to respond, to react"), the same reading it takes in 应付 (also in this batch) and 反应 ("reaction") — not the yīng reading used in 应该 ("should"), a distinction worth tracking since the character 应 covers both senses depending on tone.

components.note: 亻 (a person) — someone receiving something
寸 (a hand) — a hand handing something over

example.hanzi: 面对突然的问题,他很难应付。
example.pinyin: Miànduì tūrán de wèntí, tā hěn nán yìngfu.
example.english: Faced with the sudden problem, he found it hard to cope.
example.fact: 应付 can carry a slightly negative shade beyond a neutral "to deal with" — 应付了事 is a set phrase meaning to handle something half-heartedly just to get it over with, so 应付 alone can hint at reluctant or perfunctory effort depending on context.

components.note: 牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.
口 (mouth), stacked three times — many mouths talking about or judging something, the source of 品's meaning 'product, item; quality, rank.'

example.hanzi: 请不要在这里放置私人物品。
example.pinyin: Qǐng búyào zài zhèlǐ fàngzhì sīrén wùpǐn.
example.english: Please do not place personal belongings here.
example.fact: 品 by itself already means "item, product" and stacks three 口 ("mouth") shapes — traditionally read as many people judging or grading something together — which is also why 品 alone can mean "quality, grade," as in 人品 ("moral character").

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坏 relates to something crumbling or deteriorating, like broken soil.
不 (bù) reflects an old phonetic link that has largely faded in the modern pronunciation huài.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 电影里的坏人最后被警察抓住了。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de huàirén zuìhòu bèi jǐngchá zhuāzhù le.
example.english: In the end, the villain in the movie was caught by the police.
example.fact: 坏人 simply pairs 坏 ("bad, broken") with 人 ("person") — about as transparent as Chinese compounds get — and it names a moral judgment about someone's character, distinct from the more casual, almost playful insult 坏蛋 ("bad egg").

components.note: 臼 pictures a clay mortar or vessel.
殳 (a tool, held in a hand) strikes it, giving 毁 its meaning 'to destroy, to smash.'
一 (a horizontal line) depicts something laid over the fire below.
火 (fire) — covering a flame to smother it gave 灭 its meaning 'to extinguish, to go out.'

example.hanzi: 一场大火几乎毁灭了整座森林。
example.pinyin: Yì chǎng dàhuǒ jīhū huǐmiè le zhěng zuò sēnlín.
example.english: A huge fire almost destroyed the entire forest.
example.fact: 毁灭 doubles up two independent "destruction" verbs — 毁 ("to smash, to wreck") and 灭 ("to extinguish, to wipe out," literally a flame smothered under a cover) — into one intensified word for total, often irreversible destruction.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诅 (to curse) is done through speech.
且 (qiě) gives a sound only distantly related to zǔ today, a connection that has faded over roughly three millennia of sound change.

example.hanzi: 她诅咒那个骗她钱的人。
example.pinyin: Tā zǔzhòu nàge piàn tā qián de rén.
example.english: She cursed the person who swindled her out of money.
example.fact: Both halves point to speech: 诅 carries the 讠 ("speech") radical, and 咒 is traditionally analyzed as two stacked 口 ("mouth," suggesting chanting) above 兄 — together underscoring that 诅咒 specifically means invoking a curse through spoken ritual words, not just a casual insult.

meanings: expression or emotion showing in one's eyes

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.
礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 她的眼神里充满了担心。
example.pinyin: Tā de yǎnshén lǐ chōngmǎn le dānxīn.
example.english: Her eyes were full of worry.
example.fact: 神 here keeps its core sense of "spirit, vitality" rather than its more common "god, deity" meaning — 眼神 literally reads as "eye spirit," the animating look that shows through someone's eyes, the same 神 found in 精神 ("spirit, energy").

components.note: 十 (ten) — suggests something repeated many times.
口 (mouth) — a story passed down through ten generations of mouths gave 古 its meaning 'old, ancient.'

example.hanzi: 这座老房子看起来很古怪。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò lǎo fángzi kàn qǐlai hěn gǔguài.
example.english: This old house looks very strange.
example.fact: 古怪 pairs 古 ("old, ancient") with 怪 ("strange, odd") — something unusually old-fashioned or out of step with the times reads as simply "strange," a small window into how "outdated" and "odd" overlap in the word's origin.

components.note: 贝 (shell) — ancient Chinese currency was made from cowrie shells, linking 贝 to wealth
才 (cái) gives the sound — an exact match with 财's reading cái
厂 (chǎng) gives a hint of the sound — 产 is pronounced chǎn, nearly identical apart from the final consonant.

example.hanzi: 他把所有财产都留给了孩子。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ suǒyǒu cáichǎn dōu liú gěi le háizi.
example.english: He left all his property to his children.
example.fact: 财 carries the 贝 ("cowrie shell") radical seen across many wealth-related characters (贵 "expensive," 购 "to purchase," 贫 "poor") — a fossil of the era when shells functioned as currency in ancient China, long before coined money.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) gives a close sound cue — 进 is pronounced jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.
攵 (an action/to strike) — 攻 relates directly to attacking or striking
工 (gōng) gives the sound — 攻 is also pronounced gōng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 敌军决定在黎明前发起进攻。
example.pinyin: Díjūn juédìng zài límíng qián fāqǐ jìngōng.
example.english: The enemy army decided to launch an attack before dawn.
example.fact: 进攻 literally combines "to advance" (进) with "to strike" (攻) — a transparent military compound that extends naturally to sports commentary, where 进攻 is simply the standard word for "offense" as opposed to 防守 ("defense").

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 然 originally described burning; the meaning later shifted to 'so, correct' as 然 became a grammatical particle.
肰 (rán) gives the sound — 然 is also pronounced rán, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 他很努力,然而结果并不理想。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn nǔlì, rán'ér jiéguǒ bìng bù lǐxiǎng.
example.english: He worked very hard; however, the result wasn't ideal.
example.fact: 然而 sits at the more formal, written end of Chinese's "but" words — closer in weight to 但是 than to the casual spoken 不过 — which is why it shows up constantly in essays and news reports but can sound a touch stiff in casual conversation.

meanings: to go to a lot of trouble

components.note: 辛 is traditionally read as a picture of a hot branding iron, once used to mark prisoners — a harsh origin behind its meaning 'bitter, laborious.'
艹 (grass/plant) — 苦 relates to the bitter taste of certain plants and herbs
古 (gǔ) gives a sound close to 苦's reading kǔ

example.hanzi: 谢谢你,这段时间辛苦你了。
example.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ, zhè duàn shíjiān xīnkǔ nǐ le.
example.english: Thank you, you've worked hard this whole time.
example.fact: 辛苦你了 is a fixed, almost ritual phrase Chinese speakers use to acknowledge someone else's effort on their behalf — closer to "thanks for all your hard work" than a word-for-word translation of "bitter and hard," and it's commonly said to service staff, colleagues, or family with no exact English equivalent.

components.note: 水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.
平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.

example.hanzi: 他的英语水平提高了很多。
example.pinyin: Tā de Yīngyǔ shuǐpíng tígāo le hěn duō.
example.english: His English level has improved a lot.
example.fact: 平 alone already pictures a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — 水平 layers 水 ("water") onto that image of flatness, since still water is the clearest natural example of a perfectly level surface, and the compound then extended figuratively to mean a "standard" or "degree of skill."

components.note: 土 (earth) — 型 originally related to a mold made of clay used for casting
刑 (xíng) gives the sound — 型 is also pronounced xíng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 她换了一个新发型。
example.pinyin: Tā huàn le yí gè xīn fàxíng.
example.english: She got a new hairstyle.
example.fact: 发 is one of Chinese's most notorious tone-dependent characters: read fā it means "to send out, to emit" (发送, 出发), but read fà it narrows specifically to "hair" (发型, 头发) — the simplified script merged what were two entirely different traditional characters, 發 and 髮, into this single simplified form.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
斤 (an axe) — cutting through something.
米 (grain, in the simplified form; a bundle of thread in the traditional 斷) — the material being cut, giving 断 its meaning 'to break off, cut, sever.'

example.hanzi: 请不要打断我说话。
example.pinyin: Qǐng búyào dǎduàn wǒ shuōhuà.
example.english: Please don't interrupt me while I'm talking.
example.fact: 打断 extends 打 ("to hit") well beyond physical striking — the same "打 + verb" pattern that turns 打 into a light, almost meaningless helper verb shows up across dozens of common words (打电话 "to make a call," 打扫 "to clean") — though 打断 keeps a literal edge closer to the original "hit," since interrupting speech or breaking a bone both involve a forceful, sudden stop.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'
亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'

example.hanzi: 他决定不对同事的批评进行报复。
example.pinyin: Tā juédìng bú duì tóngshì de pīpíng jìnxíng bàofù.
example.english: He decided not to retaliate against his colleague's criticism.
example.fact: 报 carries a core sense of "to repay, to respond in kind" seen across several words (报答 "to repay a kindness," 报恩 "to repay a debt of gratitude") — 报复 applies that same "paying back" logic to injury rather than kindness, framing revenge as settling a debt.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — arguing is done vocally.
少 (shǎo) gives a sound fairly close to chǎo, sharing the rhyme.
木 (wood) — racks and frames like 架 were traditionally built of wood.
加 (jiā) gives a rhyme close to jià, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 他们昨天因为一点小事吵架了。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zuótiān yīnwèi yìdiǎn xiǎoshì chǎojià le.
example.english: They quarreled yesterday over a small matter.
example.fact: 架 in 吵架 keeps its sense of a "frame, structure" — the same 架 in 打架 ("to fight," literally "to hit a frame") and 架子 ("shelf, frame") — an old metaphor picturing a quarrel as something with its own scaffolding being built up between two people.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
正 (zhèng) gives a sound hint — 整 is pronounced zhěng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

example.hanzi: 我一整天都在写报告。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yìzhěngtiān dōu zài xiě bàogào.
example.english: I spent the whole day writing the report.
example.fact: 整 contributes "whole, complete, orderly" (as in 整齐 "neat" and 完整 "complete") — 一整天 emphasizes that literally not one hour of the day was left out, a stronger and more deliberate phrase than the plain 一天 ("one day").

components.note: 卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'
衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match

example.hanzi: 这家店专卖儿童服装。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn zhuānmài értóng fúzhuāng.
example.english: This shop specializes in children's clothing.
example.fact: 服装 sits at a more formal register than the everyday 衣服 ("clothes") — 服装 shows up in store names and fashion-industry terms (服装设计 "fashion design"), while 衣服 is what people actually say when talking about the clothes in their closet.

components.note: 亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 老师今天布置了很多作业。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī jīntiān bùzhì le hěn duō zuòyè.
example.english: The teacher assigned a lot of homework today.
example.fact: 作业 covers both a student's "homework" and a more general "task, operation" in technical or industrial contexts (施工作业 "construction work") — the same word spans a school desk and a construction site, unified by 业's core sense of an undertaking or occupation.

components.note: 高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.
纟 (thread) — 级 originally named a strand or rank of silk thread, extended to 'grade, level, rank.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 级 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这是一家非常高级的餐厅。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì jiā fēicháng gāojí de cāntīng.
example.english: This is a very high-end restaurant.
example.fact: 级 originally named a strand or rank of silk thread (its 纟 radical still carries that "thread" sense) — the image of individual threads ranked by grade extended naturally to today's meaning "level, grade, rank," the same logic behind words like 年级 ("grade level in school").

components.note: 丬 (a stylized bed) — 将 originally pictured someone preparing for bed at night.
夕 (evening/night) — the coming of night was seen as predictable, giving 将 its meaning 'about to' or 'going to' happen.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 他将来想当一名医生。
example.pinyin: Tā jiānglái xiǎng dāng yì míng yīshēng.
example.english: In the future, he wants to become a doctor.
example.fact: 将来 and its near-synonym 未来 both mean "the future," but 将来 leans toward a nearer future tied to someone's own plans, while 未来 reads as more general or distant — a nuance easy to miss since English "future" covers both without distinction.

components.note: 心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 老师对学生一直很有耐心。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī duì xuésheng yìzhí hěn yǒu nàixīn.
example.english: The teacher has always been very patient with the students.
example.fact: 耐心 pairs 耐 ("to endure, to withstand," as in 耐用 "durable") with 心 ("heart, mind") — literally "an enduring heart" — the same 耐 that describes a durable material describes a durable temperament when applied to patience.

meanings: Europe (abbr. for 歐羅巴洲|欧罗巴洲[Ou1 luo2 ba1 Zhou1])

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water surrounding the land
州 (a stretch of land) — depicted as islands of land within a river

example.hanzi: 他计划暑假去欧洲旅行。
example.pinyin: Tā jìhuà shǔjià qù Ōuzhōu lǚxíng.
example.english: He's planning to travel to Europe during summer vacation.
example.fact: 洲 is the standard suffix for continents in Chinese — 亚洲 (Asia), 非洲 (Africa), and 美洲 (the Americas) all end the same way — while 欧 itself is purely a phonetic syllable borrowed to represent the "Eu-" sound of "Europe," carrying no meaning of its own.

components.note: 阝 (hill) — 险 originally referred to steep, dangerous terrain
佥 (qiān) gives a sound distantly related to 险's reading xiǎn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 投资股票总是有一定的风险。
example.pinyin: Tóuzī gǔpiào zǒngshì yǒu yídìng de fēngxiǎn.
example.english: Investing in stocks always carries a certain amount of risk.
example.fact: 险 alone already means "danger, precipitous" (its 阝 radical points to the steep, treacherous terrain in its original sense) — adding 风 ("wind") on top gives learners a handy image of risk as an unpredictable danger that can shift like the weather, though this pairing is best treated as a descriptive gloss rather than a documented historical origin.

meanings: (Internet slang) first reply to a forum post

components.note: 氵 (water) — sand forms as water erodes rock over time.
少 (shǎo) shares the initial sh- with shā, though the vowel has since shifted.

example.hanzi: 他懒懒地躺在沙发上看电视。
example.pinyin: Tā lǎnlǎn de tǎng zài shāfā shàng kàn diànshì.
example.english: He lazily lay on the sofa watching TV.
example.fact: 沙发 is a phonetic loanword for "sofa," with 发 borrowed purely for its fā sound and no connection to its usual meanings ("hair" or "to send out") — Chinese Internet slang later reused the same two characters for an unrelated joke, "grabbing the sofa" (占沙发), meaning to post the very first reply in an online discussion thread.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.
女 (woman) — a component whose original link to the meaning has faded, an example of how radicals don't always map cleanly onto meaning.
干 (gān) gives a sound moderately close to jiān, sharing the final but not the initial.

example.hanzi: 那个案件的被告被指控强奸。
example.pinyin: Nàge ànjiàn de bèigào bèi zhǐkòng qiángjiān.
example.english: The defendant in that case was accused of rape.
example.fact: 强 here keeps its core sense of "by force, forcibly" (as in 强迫 "to force, to coerce") rather than its more common meaning "strong" — legal Chinese consistently uses 强奸 as the formal, neutral term in statutes and court documents rather than a euphemism.

components.note: 田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'

example.hanzi: 他没有考虑后果就做了决定。
example.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu kǎolǜ hòuguǒ jiù zuò le juédìng.
example.english: He made the decision without considering the consequences.
example.fact: 果 keeps its literal sense of "fruit" even here — 后果 pictures consequences as the "fruit that comes after" an action, almost always used for a negative or undesirable outcome rather than a neutral or positive one.

components.note: 芒 (the tip of a plant, an awn) — 荒 relates to overgrown, uncultivated land.
川 (chuān) gives a sound distantly related to huāng, having drifted apart over time.
讠 (speech) — 谬 relates to a false or mistaken statement.
翏 (liù) gives a sound only distantly related to miù today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这个理由听起来非常荒谬。
example.pinyin: Zhège lǐyóu tīng qǐlai fēicháng huāngmiù.
example.english: This reason sounds extremely absurd.
example.fact: 荒 contributes a sense of "wild, overgrown, uncultivated" (as in 荒地 "wasteland") and 谬 means "mistaken, erroneous" — 荒谬 combines them into an idea one step past a simple mistake: a claim so far off from reason that it reads as wildly, almost comically wrong.

components.note: 丨 (a vertical tally mark) over 人 (person) — suggests counting people one by one, fitting 个's role today as Mandarin's most common general measure word.
忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 这个孩子从小就很有个性。
example.pinyin: Zhège háizi cóngxiǎo jiù hěn yǒu gèxìng.
example.english: This child has had a lot of personality since childhood.
example.fact: 个性 specifically highlights the distinctive traits that set one person apart from others — its close relative 性格 covers someone's overall temperament more broadly, so 有个性 ("to have personality") praises someone's distinctiveness in a way 性格 alone doesn't quite capture.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 最 pictures something happening under the sun, that is, everywhere.
取 (to take, gather) — combined with the sun above, gathering everything under the sun gave 最 its meaning of 'most' or 'the utmost.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 你最好现在就出发,不然会迟到。
example.pinyin: Nǐ zuìhǎo xiànzài jiù chūfā, bùrán huì chídào.
example.english: You'd better leave right now, or you'll be late.
example.fact: Beyond its plain sense "best," 最好 doubles as a softened suggestion meaning "had better," similar to how English "best" shows up in "you'd best leave now" — in this second use it's less a superlative and more a gentle warning about what happens if the advice isn't followed.

components.note: 田 (field) — represents farmland.
力 (strength/effort) — someone strong enough to work the fields gave 男 its meaning 'male, man.'
忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 这项工作男性和女性都可以申请。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng gōngzuò nánxìng hé nǚxìng dōu kěyǐ shēnqǐng.
example.english: Both men and women can apply for this job.
example.fact: 男性 is the clinical, formal term for biological sex used on official forms and in medical or demographic contexts — everyday speech almost always prefers the plainer 男人 ("man") instead, the same formal/informal split seen between 女性 and 女人.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
隹 (a bird) — one of a flock.
木 (a tree) — birds flocking together on a tree, the image of gathering that gave 集 its meaning 'to gather, collect; a collection.'

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢收集邮票。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan shōují yóupiào.
example.english: He has liked collecting stamps since childhood.
example.fact: 集 pictures a bird (隹) perched in a tree (木) — originally suggesting birds flocking together — and that image of many separate things gathering into one place carries directly into modern words like 收集 ("to collect"), 集市 ("market"), and even 集 for a TV episode (第一集 "episode one").

components.note: Depicts a person standing with legs crossed — the crossing shape gave 交 its meaning 'to intersect, exchange, hand over.'
彳 (step/walk) — relates directly to 往's meaning 'to go toward, in the direction of.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound hint — 往 is pronounced wǎng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他们交往三年后决定结婚。
example.pinyin: Tāmen jiāowǎng sān nián hòu juédìng jiéhūn.
example.english: After dating for three years, they decided to get married.
example.fact: 交往 spans a spectrum from plain "social contact" to specifically "romantic dating," and context alone decides which sense applies — 和他交往 could mean simply "to associate with him" or "to date him," a genuine ambiguity that doesn't exist in English's separate words.

components.note: A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

example.hanzi: 他二十五岁就当上了中尉。
example.pinyin: Tā èrshíwǔ suì jiù dāng shàng le zhōngwèi.
example.english: He became a lieutenant at the age of twenty-five.
example.fact: Chinese military ranks stack 中 ("middle") between 少 ("junior") and 上 ("senior") across a whole parallel rank system — 少尉/中尉/上尉 (second lieutenant/lieutenant/captain) mirrors 少校/中校/上校 (major/lieutenant colonel/colonel) one tier up, so learning this 少-中-上 pattern once unlocks several rank names at once.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching to take hold of something.
耳 (ear) — from an ancient battlefield practice of taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill, the origin of 取's meaning 'to take, obtain.'
寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'

example.hanzi: 她通过努力取得了很好的成绩。
example.pinyin: Tā tōngguò nǔlì qǔdé le hěn hǎo de chéngjì.
example.english: Through hard work, she achieved very good grades.
example.fact: 取得 doubles up two independent "to obtain" verbs — 取 (traditionally linked to taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill in ancient battle) and 得 (a hand reaching for a valuable shell) — into one formal verb reserved for achievements or results (取得成功, 取得学位), rarely used for grabbing a simple physical object.

components.note: 上 (top) — the upper edge pressing down
卜 — the lower edge, with a card squeezed between the two

example.hanzi: 卡尔是我们班唯一的德国学生。
example.pinyin: Kǎ'ěr shì wǒmen bān wéiyī de Déguó xuésheng.
example.english: Karl is the only German student in our class.
example.fact: 卡尔 is a phonetic transliteration of the Western name "Karl/Carl" with no meaning intended — the same 卡 syllable, chosen purely for its kǎ sound, also shows up transliterating "card" (卡片, informally just 卡) and dozens of other loanwords, since it carries no strong native meaning of its own to get in the way.

components.note: 攵 (an action/to strike) — ties to 致's sense of bringing about or causing an effect
至 (zhì) gives the sound — 致 is also pronounced zhì, an exact match
令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'

example.hanzi: 那次车祸对他造成了致命的伤害。
example.pinyin: Nà cì chēhuò duì tā zàochéng le zhìmìng de shānghài.
example.english: That car accident caused him a fatal injury.
example.fact: 致 carries a sense of "to cause, to bring about" (as in 致使 "to cause, to result in") — 致命 literally means "to bring about death" — and that same formal 致 also opens the salutation of a letter (致 + recipient, "To So-and-so"), a very different register from the deadly compound it forms here.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng

example.hanzi: 中国成功发射了一颗新卫星。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó chénggōng fāshè le yì kē xīn wèixīng.
example.english: China successfully launched a new satellite.
example.fact: 卫 carries the sense "to guard, to defend" (as in 保卫 "to defend, to protect") — 卫星 literally means "guard star," picturing a satellite as a small body that stands watch in orbit around its larger companion, whether that's a planet's moon or a man-made craft circling Earth.

components.note: 月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.
Depicts a person standing tall, gazing up at the moon 月 — the image of looking into the distance, the source of 望's meaning 'to gaze, hope, expect.'

example.hanzi: 父母对他的期望很高。
example.pinyin: Fùmǔ duì tā de qīwàng hěn gāo.
example.english: His parents have high expectations of him.
example.fact: 望 pictures a person standing tall, straining to gaze into the distance at the moon — the same character that means "to look toward" extends naturally to "hope, to expect," since both involve looking ahead toward something not yet present, a link 期望 makes explicit by pairing it with 期 ("a period of time").

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嘲 relates to speaking, in this case mocking someone.
朝 (cháo) gives the sound — an exact match with 嘲.
夭 (a person leaning back) — the pose of someone laughing.
⺮ (bamboo-like strokes) — suggesting a wide grin, giving 笑 its meaning 'to laugh, smile.'

example.hanzi: 别人嘲笑他的口音,但他并不在意。
example.pinyin: Biérén cháoxiào tā de kǒuyīn, dàn tā bìng bú zàiyì.
example.english: Other people mocked his accent, but he didn't mind at all.
example.fact: 笑 alone is neutral or even warm ("to laugh, to smile"), but 嘲笑 flips the tone by combining it with 嘲 — a character whose 口 ("mouth") component and long-attested sense of jeering turn simple laughter into laughter aimed at someone. 笑 by itself never implies cruelty; it's 嘲 doing that work in this pair.

components.note: 立 depicts a person standing with arms and legs spread, on a horizontal line representing the ground — a simple picture of standing upright.
卩 (a kneeling figure) — a hungry person kneeling down, about to eat.
皀 (a bowl of food) — the meal in front of them, giving 即 its sense of imminent action, 'right away, that is to say.'

example.hanzi: 接到消息后,他立即赶往医院。
example.pinyin: Jiēdào xiāoxi hòu, tā lìjí gǎnwǎng yīyuàn.
example.english: After receiving the news, he immediately rushed to the hospital.
example.fact: 立即 pairs 立 ("to stand") with 即 ("right away, upon"), as if picturing something happening the instant one stands up — though 即 alone already means "immediately" (即刻), so 立 mainly reinforces the urgency. 立即 also sits at a more formal, written register than the everyday 马上, showing up constantly in official announcements and news reports.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 避 means to avoid, moving away from something.
辟 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 避.

example.hanzi: 为了避免迟到,他提早出门了。
example.pinyin: Wèile bìmiǎn chídào, tā tízǎo chūmén le.
example.english: To avoid being late, he left home early.
example.fact: 避免 doubles up two overlapping "to avoid" verbs — 避 ("to evade, to dodge," sharing its 辟 phonetic with 僻 "remote, secluded") and 免 ("to escape from, to be exempt from," as in 免费 "free of charge") — reinforcing each other into the strong, general-purpose verb Chinese uses for avoiding almost any undesirable situation.
